item.name: Read me first
item.description:
Docs version 1.9.0 (2026-11-23)

# Tayari API v1

One API for three apps: the **Flutter app** (customers and business owners on mobile), the **React website** (customers and businesses on the web) and the **React admin panel** (Tayari staff). Every endpoint in this collection sits in the folder of the app that uses it, next to the screen that calls it.

## Base URL and versions

- All endpoints start with `{{baseUrl}}` = `{{appUrl}}/api/v1` (for example `http://localhost:8000/api/v1`).
- `v1` stays stable. A breaking change gets a new version (`/api/v2`); old apps keep working on `v1` until they update.
- **426 Upgrade Required** means this mobile app version is too old: show the force-update screen and send the user to the store. It only happens on Android and iOS, never on the web.

## Headers on every request

- `Accept: application/json`: always send it, so every answer is JSON.
- `Accept-Language: ar` or `en`: the language of every message and of translated names (for example business types). Anything else, or no header, means Arabic.
- `X-Platform: android`, `ios` or `web`: which app is calling.
- `X-App-Version` (mobile only, for example `1.4.0`): the installed app version. The server compares it with the minimum version and answers **426** when it is lower.

This collection adds these headers for you (see the scripts on the app folders).

## How each app logs in

- **Flutter app:** `POST auth/token` returns a **Bearer token**. Store it securely and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every request. Logout deletes it on the server.
- **React website and admin panel:** a **session cookie** (Laravel Sanctum). First call `GET {{appUrl}}/sanctum/csrf-cookie`, then `POST auth/login`. Send every request with cookies (`credentials: 'include'` in fetch, `withCredentials: true` in axios) and the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header taken from the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie (axios does this by itself). The website must run on a domain the server trusts (`SANCTUM_STATEFUL_DOMAINS`).
- **Postman setup for the React folders:** open **Cookies › Domains Allowlist** and add the host of `{{appUrl}}` (for example `localhost`). Otherwise the folder script can't read the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie and requests answer **419**. The Postman console shows a warning when this is missing.

## Errors

Every error has the same shape:

```json
{
  "message": "A short message for the user, in the request language.",
  "errors": { "phone": ["The phone number field is required."] }
}
```

- Show each `errors.<field>` message under its input.
- Show `message` in a toast, snackbar or dialog. `errors` is an empty object when there are no field errors.

## Status codes every app must handle

- **200, 201, 204:** success (201 = created, 204 = success with no body).
- **401:** not logged in, or the token or session expired. Clear the stored login and go to the Login screen.
- **403:** the account is blocked, the phone is not verified, or the user isn't allowed to do this. Show `message` as it is.
- **404:** not found. Show a "not found" state.
- **419 (web only):** the CSRF cookie is missing or old. Call `sanctum/csrf-cookie` again and retry once.
- **422:** invalid input. Show `errors` under the fields.
- **426 (mobile only):** force update.
- **429:** too many attempts. Most limits are per phone number and per IP address (users on the same network share the IP limit); login counts tries per phone number from the same IP address, plus an hourly limit per phone number. Wait (see the `Retry-After` header, in seconds) and let the user retry.
- **500:** something went wrong on the server. Show a generic error and let the user retry.

## Lists and pages

Lists are paginated. Send `page` (starts at 1) and `per_page` (default 20, at most 100). The answer has:

- `data`: the items of this page;
- `meta`: `current_page`, `last_page`, `per_page`, `total`, `from`, `to`;
- `links`: `first`, `last`, `prev` and `next` URLs (`next` is null on the last page).

A few long lists (for example **Get my orders**) use **cursor pages** instead: send `cursor` = `meta.next_cursor` from the previous answer (and `per_page`) until `next_cursor` is null. Their `meta` has `per_page`, `next_cursor` and `prev_cursor`, with no total.

## Language, dates and documents

- Messages and translated names follow `Accept-Language`. The language at sign up is saved on the account and used for SMS.
- All dates are UTC in ISO 8601 (for example `2026-11-21T09:30:00Z`). Convert them to the user's time zone before showing them.
- Personal and business documents are private. API responses include a short signed `url` for each file, valid for 5 minutes. Open it as it is; when it expires, load the screen data again to get a new URL.
- Phone numbers can be typed in any Egyptian mobile format (`010…`, `+2010…`, Arabic digits). The server saves and returns them as `+201XXXXXXXXX`.

## Demo accounts

Fake accounts for trying every screen. They exist only on a server where `php artisan db:seed --class=DemoDataSeeder` was run with `DEMO_USERS_PASSWORD` set to the password below, and they are wiped before launch. Never use them for real orders.

- **Password of every demo account:** `DFT5sxvmezNBWL8g` (`{{demo_password}}` in the **Tayari Local** environment).
- **Phones:** each account has an environment variable, for example `{{demo_tayar_approved_phone}}`. Log in with the phone as shown; the server accepts any Egyptian format.
- **Which app uses which account:** Admin panel: the three staff accounts. Website: the business accounts. Flutter app: the tayar and business accounts.
- The approved business (`{{demo_business_approved_phone}}`) has three demo orders in Nasr City and Downtown: one looking for a tayar, one cancelled food order, and one the approved tayar accepted, picked up and brought on the way (`ongoing`). On a local server (`APP_ENV=local`, log SMS driver) the receiver's codes for that order are in `storage/logs/laravel.log` (search for `SMS sent`); on other servers receivers get codes only once a real SMS provider is configured. The order looking for a tayar is cancelled by the system 15 minutes after seeding when the scheduler runs.
- The approved tayar (`{{demo_tayar_approved_phone}}`) is online in the area mode in Nasr City after seeding (until the server sets them offline for sending no location). They hold the accepted demo order, the most the area mode allows, so they get no new offers until staff cancel that order from the admin panel.
- The rejected tayar can change the application from `can_reapply_at` (after TAYAR_REAPPLY_AFTER_HOURS, 24 hours by default).

## Endpoints no app calls directly

- `GET /api/v1/media/{media}`: Private documents are only opened through the short signed `url` the API returns (for example in `auth/me` or a business profile). Use that URL as it is, in an image view, a PDF viewer or a new tab; never build it yourself.

item.description:
## 1.9.0 (2026-11-23)

- Added: POST /api/v1/tayar/orders/{order}/pickup — confirms the pickup of an accepted order with 1 to 4 photos (multipart) and lat/lng: the order becomes picked_up, and the receiver gets the delivery and refusal codes and the tracking link in one SMS (only hashes are stored); 422 errors.status when another step is due. Apps: Flutter tayar mode.
- Added: POST /api/v1/tayar/orders/{order}/receiver-confirmed — the receiver confirmed by phone they are there today: the order becomes ongoing (lat/lng required). Apps: Flutter tayar mode.
- Added: POST /api/v1/tayar/orders/{order}/deliver — delivers an ongoing order with the receiver's delivery code: 422 errors.code for a wrong code (shared count of 5 with the refusal step, then locked until new codes are sent), expired codes (24 hours) or codes not sent yet; 429 after 10 codes a minute. Delivery does not check payment yet (the payment phase comes later), and receivers get codes only once a real SMS provider is configured. Apps: Flutter tayar mode.
- Added: POST /api/v1/tayar/orders/{order}/not-delivered — the receiver refused at the door: the refusal code, a not_delivered reason and an optional note make the order not_delivered (final; returns come later). Same code rules as deliver. Apps: Flutter tayar mode.
- Added: POST /api/v1/admin/orders/{order}/not-delivered — staff (orders.manage) close a picked_up or ongoing order as not_delivered without a code, with a required reason and note, when the receiver can't be reached; the sender and the tayar both get an order_not_delivered push. The only status staff can force. Apps: Admin panel.
- Added: POST /api/v1/admin/orders/{order}/resend-codes — staff (orders.manage) send the receiver new codes by SMS (204); the old codes stop working and the wrong-code count restarts. Apps: Admin panel.
- Added: GET /api/v1/track/{trackingToken} — the receiver's public tracking page (no login, 30 requests a minute per IP): status, business name, the tayar's first name and vehicle, and the last position while picked_up or ongoing; no phones, codes or amounts; keeps answering with the final status after the order ends. Apps: Website.
- Added: POST /api/v1/track/{trackingToken}/resend-codes — sends the receiver new codes by SMS while the order is picked_up or ongoing (204; 3 an hour per order); the codes are never shown on the page. Delivery does not check payment yet (the payment phase comes later), and receivers get codes only once a real SMS provider is configured. Apps: Website.
- Changed: POST /api/v1/client/orders — the order has the new fields tracking_token, tayar.location, pickup_photos, picked_up_at, receiver_confirmed_at, codes_sent_at, delivered_at, not_delivered_at, not_delivered_reason and not_delivered_note. Apps: Website, Flutter client mode.
- Changed: GET /api/v1/client/orders — the same new order fields; tayar.location is the tayar's last position while pending, picked_up or ongoing. Apps: Website, Flutter client mode.
- Changed: GET /api/v1/client/orders/{order} — the same new order fields; poll every 10 to 15 seconds while the order is accepted, picked up or on the way; there is no ETA. Apps: Website, Flutter client mode.
- Changed: POST /api/v1/client/orders/{order}/cancel — the response has the new order fields; a picked-up order can't be cancelled (422 errors.status), as before for every status after pending. Apps: Website, Flutter client mode.
- Changed: POST /api/v1/tayar/offers/{offer}/accept — the returned order has the new delivery fields (pickup_photos, receiver_codes, the step timestamps, not_delivered_reason and not_delivered_note). Apps: Flutter tayar mode.
- Changed: GET /api/v1/tayar/orders — each order has the new delivery fields, including receiver_codes (sent_at, expire_at, attempts_left, problem; never the codes). Apps: Flutter tayar mode.
- Changed: GET /api/v1/tayar/orders/{order} — the new delivery fields, including receiver_codes. Apps: Flutter tayar mode.
- Changed: POST /api/v1/tayar/offline — refused with 422 errors.status while the tayar holds an accepted, picked-up or ongoing order; the stale-location job also leaves such a tayar online. Apps: Flutter tayar mode.
- Changed: PATCH /api/v1/auth/mode — switching to client mode is refused with 422 errors.status while the tayar holds an accepted, picked-up or ongoing order, even when the tayar is already offline. Apps: Flutter client mode, Flutter tayar mode.
- Changed: GET /api/v1/order-reasons — type=not_delivered now lists the not-delivered reasons, for the tayar's and staff's not-delivered dialogs. Apps: Flutter tayar mode, Admin panel.
- Changed: GET /api/v1/admin/orders — each order has the new fields picked_up_at, receiver_confirmed_at, delivered_at, not_delivered_at, not_delivered_reason, not_delivered_note, tracking_token and receiver_codes (sent_at, expire_at, attempts, locked; never the codes). Apps: Admin panel.
- Changed: GET /api/v1/admin/orders/{order} — the same new fields plus pickup_photos, and status_history rows now have lat and lng (where the tayar was). Apps: Admin panel.
- Changed: POST /api/v1/admin/orders/{order}/cancel — the response has the new order fields; staff can't cancel a picked-up order (422 errors.status): close it as not delivered instead. Apps: Admin panel.
- Docs: Flutter folder 4. Push notifications — lists the new push types order_picked_up, order_on_the_way and order_delivered (sender; order_id) and order_not_delivered (sender, and the tayar when staff close the order; order_id). Apps: Flutter client mode, Flutter tayar mode.
- Docs: Flutter folder 17. Tayar mode · Delivery — pickup photos, calling the receiver, the delivery and refusal codes, lock-out, and "receiver unreachable: contact support, who closes the order". Apps: Flutter tayar mode.
- Docs: Website folder 8. Tracking page — the receiver's public tracking page and the resend-codes button. Apps: Website.
- Docs: Read me first — the demo order the approved tayar accepted is now on the way (ongoing), and on a local server its receiver codes can be read from the log. Apps: Website, Admin panel, Flutter client mode, Flutter tayar mode.

## 1.8.0 (2026-11-23)

- Added: GET /api/v1/tayar/offers — my live offers for the current work session (cursor pages): the trip without phone numbers, my tayar_earning, expires_at and expires_in_seconds; poll every 5 to 10 seconds while online. Apps: Flutter tayar mode.
- Added: POST /api/v1/tayar/offers/{offer}/accept — accepts an offer: 200 with the order (now pending, with the sender and receiver phones), also for a second tap while the order is still mine and pending; when the accept brings the tayar to the mode's limit, the tayar's other open offers are withdrawn; 422 errors.offer when the offer expired, another tayar took the order, the work session ended, or the tayar holds as many orders as the mode allows; 403 for another tayar's offer. Apps: Flutter tayar mode.
- Added: POST /api/v1/tayar/offers/{offer}/reject — rejects an offer (no reason): 204, and the order is never offered to this tayar again. Apps: Flutter tayar mode.
- Added: GET /api/v1/tayar/orders — the orders I accepted, status=active (default) or past, with cursor pages; each with cancel_fee when the sender owes me one for a late cancel; the sender, pickup contact and receiver phones are null once an order is past (the names stay). Apps: Flutter tayar mode.
- Added: GET /api/v1/tayar/orders/{order} — one order I accepted, with the pickup contact, sender and receiver phones while it is active (null once it is past; the names stay), my earning, and cancel_fee when the sender owes me one for a late cancel; 403 for any other order. Apps: Flutter tayar mode.
- Added: GET /api/v1/admin/orders/{order}/offers — every offer of an order, newest first: tayar, round, distance, earning, status (offered, accepted, rejected, expired, withdrawn) and responded_at (orders.view). Apps: Admin panel.
- Changed: POST /api/v1/client/orders — the new order is offered at once to nearby tayars in its mode, in rounds; when no tayar accepts by search_ends_at, Tayari cancels it (cancelled_by_type = system) and sends an order_no_tayar push. The response has the new order fields (tayar, cancelled_by_type, search_ends_at, accepted_at). Apps: Website, Flutter client mode.
- Changed: GET /api/v1/client/orders — each order has the new fields tayar (name, phone, vehicle; null until a tayar accepts; phone null once the order is past), cancelled_by_type, search_ends_at, accepted_at, free_cancel_until, cancel_fee_now and cancel_fee; can_cancel is now true until pickup. Apps: Website, Flutter client mode.
- Changed: GET /api/v1/client/orders/{order} — the new fields tayar (phone null once the order is past), cancelled_by_type, search_ends_at, accepted_at, free_cancel_until (until when cancelling an accepted order is free), cancel_fee_now (what cancelling now costs) and cancel_fee; can_cancel is now true until pickup; poll every 10 seconds while the order is looking for a tayar. Apps: Website, Flutter client mode.
- Changed: POST /api/v1/client/orders/{order}/cancel — the sender can now cancel after a tayar accepted, until pickup: free for MATCHING_FREE_CANCEL_SECONDS (120 by default) after the accept, then a cancellation fee owed to the tayar (MATCHING_CANCEL_FEE, at most the shipping fee) is recorded on the order and returned as cancel_fee (nothing is charged yet; the wallet settles it later); the tayar gets an order_cancelled push; open offers are withdrawn; 422 errors.status only once the order is picked up. Apps: Website, Flutter client mode, Flutter tayar mode.
- Changed: GET /api/v1/admin/orders — new tayar_id filter, and the new fields tayar, vehicle, work_session_id, cancelled_by_type, cancel_fee, cancel_fee_owed_to and accepted_at; fee.tayar_earning and fee.platform_fee become the accepting tayar's on accept. Apps: Admin panel.
- Changed: GET /api/v1/admin/orders/{order} — the new fields tayar, vehicle, work_session_id, cancelled_by_type, cancel_fee, cancel_fee_owed_to (the tayar a sender's late-cancel fee is owed to) and accepted_at; can_cancel is now also true for an accepted (pending) order; a status_history row with changed_by = null is the system. Apps: Admin panel.
- Changed: POST /api/v1/admin/orders/{order}/cancel — staff can now cancel an accepted (pending) order before pickup, at any time and never with a cancellation fee; the order keeps its tayar, open offers are withdrawn, and the tayar gets an order_cancelled push. Apps: Admin panel, Flutter tayar mode.
- Docs: Flutter folder 4. Push notifications — lists the push types order_offer (tayar; order_id, offer_id), order_accepted and order_no_tayar (sender; order_id) and order_cancelled (tayar, when the sender or staff cancel an accepted order; order_id, cancelled_by_type), and which screen each opens. Apps: Flutter client mode, Flutter tayar mode.
- Docs: Flutter folders 15. Tayar mode · Offers and 16. Tayar mode · My orders — the offer cards with polling and the countdown, and the accepted orders. Apps: Flutter tayar mode.
- Docs: Read me first — the demo data now has the approved tayar online in the area mode in Nasr City and a third demo order that tayar accepted. Apps: Website, Admin panel, Flutter client mode, Flutter tayar mode.

## 1.7.0 (2026-11-23)

- Added: GET /api/v1/order-reasons — lists the active reasons of one type (type=cancel) in display order (id, name), for the cancel dialog; no login. Apps: Website, Flutter client mode, Admin panel.
- Added: POST /api/v1/client/orders/estimate — prices a trip (category_id, pickup and drop-off lat/lng) without creating an order: distance_km, food_extra and shipping_fee; approved business accounts only (403 otherwise), errors.route when the pickup and drop-off are less than 100 m apart (straight line), the trip is too long, not served, or too far for food. Apps: Website, Flutter client mode.
- Added: POST /api/v1/client/orders — creates an order in looking_for_tayar at the shipping_fee from the estimate (422 errors.shipping_fee when the price changed, errors.route as in the estimate, errors.idempotency_key when the order that key made was deleted); a required idempotency_key (UUID) makes a double tap or retry return the same order with 200 instead of a second one (201); approved business accounts only. Apps: Website, Flutter client mode.
- Added: GET /api/v1/client/orders — my orders, newest first, status=active (default) or past, with cursor pages (cursor, meta.next_cursor). Apps: Website, Flutter client mode.
- Added: GET /api/v1/client/orders/{order} — one of my orders, with can_cancel; 403 for someone else's order. Apps: Website, Flutter client mode.
- Added: POST /api/v1/client/orders/{order}/cancel — cancels my order before a tayar accepts it, with cancel_reason_id and an optional note; 422 errors.status once it can no longer be cancelled. Apps: Website, Flutter client mode.
- Added: GET /api/v1/admin/orders — every order, newest first, with status, sender_id, category_id, mode_id, created_from and created_to (Cairo business days) filters and a search by order code or phone, with the fee breakdown (orders.view). Apps: Admin panel.
- Added: GET /api/v1/admin/orders/{order} — one order with its fee breakdown, cancel details and full status history with who made each change (orders.view). Apps: Admin panel.
- Added: POST /api/v1/admin/orders/{order}/cancel — cancels an order before a tayar accepts it, with cancel_reason_id and an optional note (orders.manage: ops, admin, super admin). Apps: Admin panel.
- Changed: GET /api/v1/auth/me — permissions can now include orders.view (support, ops, admin) and orders.manage (ops, admin), to show the Orders menu and the Cancel button. Apps: Admin panel.
- Docs: Read me first — lists with cursor pages are explained, and the demo accounts section notes the approved business's two demo orders (one looking for a tayar, one cancelled). Apps: Website, Admin panel, Flutter client mode.
- Docs: GET /api/v1/categories — the Categories folders now point to the new Orders folders (Website 7. Orders, Flutter 14. Client mode · Orders). Apps: Website, Flutter client mode.
- Docs: GET /api/v1/admin/pricing-rules — the notes now say new orders are priced with the mode's rule for every vehicle. Apps: Admin panel.

## 1.6.0 (2026-11-23)

- Docs: Read me first — a new Demo accounts section: the DemoDataSeeder command (php artisan db:seed --class=DemoDataSeeder), the shared demo password, and the 11 demo accounts with phone, name, kind, status, next_step and the app that uses each; they exist only where the seeder was run with that password and are wiped before launch. The Tayari Local environment adds demo_password and one variable per demo phone (demo_admin_phone to demo_tayar_new_phone). Apps: Website, Admin panel, Flutter client mode, Flutter tayar mode.

## 1.5.0 (2026-11-23)

- Added: GET /api/v1/categories — lists the active main categories, each with its active subcategories (id, name, is_food, icon_url, children), for the category picker of a new order; no login. Apps: Website, Flutter client mode.
- Added: GET /api/v1/modes — lists the active modes (id, code, name, description, allows_food, requires_area, requires_radius, requires_destination, and radius_km min and max for the zone mode) for the mode picker before going online; no login. Apps: Flutter tayar mode.
- Added: GET /api/v1/areas — lists the active areas (id, name, city, center, radius_km) for the area mode picker; no login. Apps: Flutter tayar mode.
- Breaking (before launch): POST /api/v1/tayar/online — mode_id is now required, plus area_id for the area mode, radius_km (1 to 15 km by default) for the zone mode, or destination_address, destination_lat and destination_lng for the long distance mode; a field the picked mode doesn't take is refused. Apps: Flutter tayar mode: show the Choose mode sheet (Get modes, Get areas) before Go online and send these fields.
- Changed: POST /api/v1/tayar/online — going online again with other settings (mode, area, radius or destination) ends the work session and starts a new one; the same settings still only move the position. work_session in the response now has mode (id, code, name), area, radius_km and destination. Apps: Flutter tayar mode.
- Changed: POST /api/v1/tayar/offline — work_session in the response has the new mode, area, radius_km and destination fields when present (it is null after going offline). Apps: Flutter tayar mode.
- Changed: DELETE /api/v1/admin/vehicle-types/{vehicleType} — also refused (422, errors.vehicle_type) when a pricing rule uses the type. Apps: Admin panel.
- Added: GET /api/v1/admin/categories — lists main categories and subcategories with main_only, parent_id, is_active, is_food and search filters, in sort order, with parent, icon_url and children_count. Apps: Admin panel.
- Added: GET /api/v1/admin/categories/{category} — one category with its name in both languages, its parent and its icon. Apps: Admin panel.
- Added: POST /api/v1/admin/categories — creates a main category or a subcategory (parent_id must be a main category; names unique among siblings ignoring letter case; is_food defaults to the parent's). Apps: Admin panel.
- Added: PATCH /api/v1/admin/categories/{category} — updates or moves a category; two levels at most, and a category with subcategories can't move under another one. Apps: Admin panel.
- Added: POST /api/v1/admin/categories/{category}/activate — shows the category in the public list again. Apps: Admin panel.
- Added: POST /api/v1/admin/categories/{category}/deactivate — hides the category (and a main category's subcategories) from the public list. Apps: Admin panel.
- Added: DELETE /api/v1/admin/categories/{category} — deletes a category without subcategories, with its icon; otherwise 422 asking to deactivate it instead. Apps: Admin panel.
- Added: POST /api/v1/admin/categories/{category}/icon — uploads or replaces the category icon (multipart icon: jpg, png or webp) on the public disk. Apps: Admin panel.
- Added: DELETE /api/v1/admin/categories/{category}/icon — removes the category icon. Apps: Admin panel.
- Added: GET /api/v1/admin/modes — lists the three fixed modes with is_active and search filters, with work_sessions_count. Apps: Admin panel.
- Added: GET /api/v1/admin/modes/{mode} — one mode with its name and description in both languages. Apps: Admin panel.
- Added: PATCH /api/v1/admin/modes/{mode} — updates a mode's names, description, allows_food, is_active or sort_order; the code never changes and modes can't be created or deleted. Apps: Admin panel.
- Added: POST /api/v1/admin/modes/{mode}/activate — lets tayars go online in the mode again. Apps: Admin panel.
- Added: POST /api/v1/admin/modes/{mode}/deactivate — hides the mode from the tayar's mode picker; tayars online in it keep working. Apps: Admin panel.
- Added: GET /api/v1/admin/areas — lists areas with is_active and search filters, in sort order, with work_sessions_count. Apps: Admin panel.
- Added: GET /api/v1/admin/areas/{area} — one area with its name and city in both languages. Apps: Admin panel.
- Added: POST /api/v1/admin/areas — creates an area (names and city in both languages, center_lat, center_lng, radius_km 0.5 to 50). Apps: Admin panel.

item.name: Flutter app
item.description:
The mobile app for customers, business owners and tayars (Android and iOS). One app, two modes: client mode and tayar mode (see the **Tayar mode** folders).

- **Login:** Bearer token from **Sign up and login › Log in**. Its script saves the token to `{{token}}`, and every request in this folder sends it.
- **Headers:** this folder adds `X-Platform: {{platform}}` (`android` by default; set `ios` in the environment) and `X-App-Version: {{appVersion}}`.
- Build the folders in order: app start, sign up and login, account, push notifications, then the business and national ID screens, then the **Tayar mode** folders, then **Client mode · Categories** and **Client mode · Orders**.
- **Reopening the app:** `last_mode` in **Get my account** says which mode to open (`tayar` only works while `tayar_profile.status` is `approved`).

## Onboarding

1. **Splash** → **App start** (**Get app config**).
2. **Choice** screen: **Tayar** or **Business owner** (individual customers come later).
3. **Sign up** screen: name, phone, password, password again → **Sign up** with `register_as` = `tayar` or `business`.
4. **OTP** screen when `phone_verification_required` is true → **Verify phone**, then **Log in**.
5. **Get my account**, then open the screen for `next_step`:
   - `complete_business_profile` → the business profile form (**Get business types**, **Create business profile**);
   - `business_under_review` / `business_rejected` → **Get business profile** (show `rejection_reason` when rejected);
   - `complete_tayar_application` → the tayar application form (**Get vehicle types**, **Apply to be a tayar**);
   - `tayar_under_review` / `tayar_rejected` → **Get my tayar application** (show `rejection_reason`, and allow changes from `can_reapply_at`);
   - `ready` → the home screen.
6. **Tayars:** approval doesn't change the mode. When `register_as` = `tayar`, `next_step` = `ready` and `last_mode` = `client`, call **Switch mode** with `tayar` once, then open the tayar home and **Go online**.

Always decide the screen from `next_step` after **Log in** or on app start, never from local state: it still works after a reinstall or a login on another phone.

item.name: 1. App start
item.description:
What the app does on the **Splash** screen, before anything else:

1. Call **Get app config**.
2. If the installed version is lower than `min_supported_version` for this platform, show the **force-update** screen (no way past it) with a button to the store.
3. Else, if it is lower than `latest_version`, show an **optional update** dialog ("Update" / "Later").
4. Keep `phone_verification_required`: it decides whether the OTP screen comes after sign up.
5. If a token is stored, go to Home (and call **Get my account**); otherwise go to Login.

Any other request can also answer **426** later: show the same force-update screen.

request.description:
### What it does

Returns the app settings the apps need at start: the minimum and latest app versions per platform, whether phone verification is on, and the server time.

### Screen

**Splash** screen, on every app start (and when the app comes back after a long time in the background).

### Who can call it

Anyone, no login. It is never blocked by the app version check, so an old app can always read it.

### Request

- No body or parameters. Send the usual headers.

### Success

**200** with `data`:
- `min_supported_version`: `android` and `ios` (string or null). Below it, the app must update.
- `latest_version`: `android` and `ios` (string or null). Below it, an update is available but optional.
- `phone_verification_required` (boolean): whether sign up needs the OTP step.
- `server_time`: the server time in UTC.

**Next:** Force update, optional update dialog, then Home or Login as described in the folder.

### Errors

- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Compare versions number by number (`1.10.0` is newer than `1.9.0`). Ignore a `+build` suffix.
- A null version means "no rule": don't block or suggest anything.

item.name: 2. Sign up and login
item.description:
From a new user to a logged-in user:

1. **Sign up** screen, after the **Tayar** / **Business owner** choice: name, phone, password, password again. Submit → **Sign up** with `register_as` (`tayar` or `business`).
2. If the answer has `phone_verification_required: true`, open the **OTP** screen; otherwise go to **Login**.
3. **OTP** screen: a 6-digit code input and a **Resend code** button with a countdown that starts at `resend_available_in` seconds. Submit → **Verify phone**; resend → **Resend code** (purpose `verify_phone`), then restart the countdown at 60 seconds.
4. After the phone is verified, go to **Login** (verifying does not log in).
5. **Login** screen: phone and password → **Log in**. Save the token, register the push token (**Push notifications**), then open the screen for `next_step` (see **Onboarding** in the app folder).
6. **Forgot password** screen: phone → **Forgot password**, then always open **Reset password**.
7. **Reset password** screen: code, new password, new password again → **Reset password**, then go to Login.

If Login answers 403 "verify your phone", open the OTP screen and call **Resend code** first.

request.description:
### What it does

Creates a new account. It does not log the user in.

### Screen

**Sign up** screen, when the user taps **Create account**.

### Who can call it

Guest (not logged in).

### Request

- `name` (string, required): up to 255 characters.
- `phone` (string, required): any Egyptian mobile format (`01000000000`, `+201000000000`, `00201000000000`, spaces, dashes and Arabic digits are fine). The server saves it as `+201XXXXXXXXX`.
- `password` (string, required): 8 to 64 characters.
- `password_confirmation` (string, required): the same password again.
- `register_as` (required): `business` (business owner) or `tayar`, from the choice on the first screen. Individual customers come later.
- `Accept-Language` is saved as the account language (used for SMS).

### Success

**201** with:
- `data`: the new user: `id`, `name`, `phone`, `email`, `account_type` (`individual` | `business`), `register_as` (`business` | `tayar`, or null for accounts from before sign up asked for it), `next_step` (the screen to open: see **Get my account**), `locale` (`ar` | `en`), `status` (`active` | `blocked`), `is_phone_verified`, `phone_verified_at`, `national_id` (`status`: null | `pending` | `approved` | `rejected`, `rejection_reason`, `verified_at`, `front` and `back` files with a signed `url`), `business_profile` (or null), `last_mode` (`client` | `tayar`: the mode the app reopens in), `tayar_profile` (`id`, `status`, `is_online`, `rejection_reason`, `can_reapply_at`, or null when the user never applied), `roles` (staff role names, for display only; an empty list for customers) and `permissions` (what the user may do; an empty list for customers, every permission for a super admin). `next_step` is `complete_business_profile` or `complete_tayar_application`: after the code screen and Login, open that form.
- `phone_verification_required` (boolean): when true, an SMS code was sent.
- `resend_available_in` (number of seconds, or null): how long until **Resend code** may send another code. Null when no code was sent.
- `message`: "Your account has been created."

**Next:** If `phone_verification_required` is true, open the OTP screen with the countdown from `resend_available_in`; otherwise go to Login.

### Errors

- **422:** field errors. A phone that already has an account gets `errors.phone` = "This phone number already has an account. Please log in, or use forgot password.": show it with links to Login and Forgot password.
- **429:** too many attempts from this phone number or this IP address (users on the same network share the IP limit). Wait for `Retry-After` seconds, then let the user retry.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Register never changes an existing account. An unverified user who comes back finishes with **Resend code** and **Verify phone**, not with register again.
- Limits: 5 requests per phone number and 20 per IP address every 60 minutes (users on the same network share the IP limit). **Sign up**, **Resend code** and **Forgot password** share one limit per phone.

### What it does

Confirms the phone number with the SMS code. It does not log the user in.

### Screen

**OTP** screen, when the user enters the code (or taps **Verify**).

### Who can call it

Guest.

### Request

- `phone` (string, required): any Egyptian mobile format (`01000000000`, `+201000000000`, `00201000000000`, spaces, dashes and Arabic digits are fine). The server saves it as `+201XXXXXXXXX`.
- `code` (string, required): the 6-digit code from the SMS.

### Success

**200** with `message` ("Your phone number has been verified.").

**Next:** Show "Phone verified" and go to Login.

### Errors

- **422:** The same error for a wrong code, an expired code, a used code, a code with too many wrong tries (5 per code) and an unknown phone: `errors.code` = "The code is wrong or has expired…". Show it under the code input and offer **Resend code**.
- **429:** too many attempts from this phone number or this IP address (users on the same network share the IP limit). Wait for `Retry-After` seconds, then let the user retry.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- A code is valid for 5 minutes and allows 5 wrong tries.
- Limits: 5 tries per phone number and 20 per IP address every 60 minutes (users on the same network share the IP limit). **Verify phone** and **Reset password** share one limit per phone.

### What it does

Sends a new SMS code for phone verification or for a password reset.

### Screen

**OTP** screen (purpose `verify_phone`) and **Reset password** screen (purpose `reset_password`), when the user taps **Resend code** after the countdown.

### Who can call it

Guest.

### Request

- `phone` (string, required): any Egyptian mobile format (`01000000000`, `+201000000000`, `00201000000000`, spaces, dashes and Arabic digits are fine). The server saves it as `+201XXXXXXXXX`.
- `purpose` (required): `verify_phone` or `reset_password`.

### Success

**200** with `message` ("If this phone number can receive a code, we have sent one."). Restart the resend countdown at 60 seconds.

### Errors

- **422:** field errors.
- **429:** too many attempts from this phone number or this IP address (users on the same network share the IP limit). Wait for `Retry-After` seconds, then let the user retry.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- **Same answer for registered and unknown phones**, and for an already verified phone: never tell the user whether the number has an account.
- Within 60 seconds of the last code, nothing new is sent and the earlier code stays valid. Keep the **Resend** button disabled during the countdown.
- A new code replaces the old one.
- Limits: 5 requests per phone number and 20 per IP address every 60 minutes (users on the same network share the IP limit). **Sign up**, **Resend code** and **Forgot password** share one limit per phone.

### What it does

Mobile login. Returns a Bearer token for this device.

### Screen

**Login** screen, when the user taps **Log in**.

### Who can call it

Guest.

### Request

- `phone` (string, required): any Egyptian mobile format (`01000000000`, `+201000000000`, `00201000000000`, spaces, dashes and Arabic digits are fine). The server saves it as `+201XXXXXXXXX`.
- `password` (string, required): up to 64 characters.
- `device_name` (string, required): up to 100 characters, for example the phone model. It names the token.

### Success

**200** with:
- `token`: send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every request. Store it in secure storage.
- `token_type`: `Bearer`.
- `data`: the user: `id`, `name`, `phone`, `email`, `account_type` (`individual` | `business`), `register_as` (`business` | `tayar`, or null for accounts from before sign up asked for it), `next_step` (the screen to open: see **Get my account**), `locale` (`ar` | `en`), `status` (`active` | `blocked`), `is_phone_verified`, `phone_verified_at`, `national_id` (`status`: null | `pending` | `approved` | `rejected`, `rejection_reason`, `verified_at`, `front` and `back` files with a signed `url`), `business_profile` (or null), `last_mode` (`client` | `tayar`: the mode the app reopens in), `tayar_profile` (`id`, `status`, `is_online`, `rejection_reason`, `can_reapply_at`, or null when the user never applied), `roles` (staff role names, for display only; an empty list for customers) and `permissions` (what the user may do; an empty list for customers, every permission for a super admin).

**Next:** Save `token` in secure storage, call **Save push token**, then open the screen for `data.next_step`.

### Errors

- **422:** wrong phone or password: `errors.phone` = "These credentials do not match our records." (the same for an unknown phone).
- **403:** the account is blocked, or the phone is not verified while phone verification is on. Show `message`; for "verify your phone", open the OTP screen (call **Resend code** first).
- **429:** too many login tries: 5 per minute for each phone number from the same IP address, or 20 per hour for one phone number from any IP address. Wait for `Retry-After` seconds, then let the user retry.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Limits: 5 tries per minute for each phone number from the same IP address, plus 20 per hour for each phone number from any IP address. Mobile and web login share these limits.

### What it does

Sends a password reset code by SMS.

### Screen

**Forgot password** screen, when the user taps **Send code**.

### Who can call it

Guest.

### Request

- `phone` (string, required): any Egyptian mobile format (`01000000000`, `+201000000000`, `00201000000000`, spaces, dashes and Arabic digits are fine). The server saves it as `+201XXXXXXXXX`.

### Success

**200** with `message` ("If an account exists for this phone number, we have sent it a reset code."). Always go to the Reset password screen.

**Next:** Open the Reset password screen with the phone filled in.

### Errors

- **422:** the phone is missing or not a valid Egyptian mobile number.
- **429:** too many attempts from this phone number or this IP address (users on the same network share the IP limit). Wait for `Retry-After` seconds, then let the user retry.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- **Same answer for registered and unknown phones**: never tell the user whether the number has an account.
- Always uses the SMS code, even when phone verification is off.
- Within 60 seconds of the last code, nothing new is sent and the earlier code stays valid.
- Limits: 5 requests per phone number and 20 per IP address every 60 minutes (users on the same network share the IP limit). **Sign up**, **Resend code** and **Forgot password** share one limit per phone.

### What it does

Sets a new password with the reset code from the SMS.

### Screen

**Reset password** screen, when the user taps **Save**.

### Who can call it

Guest.

### Request

- `phone` (string, required): any Egyptian mobile format (`01000000000`, `+201000000000`, `00201000000000`, spaces, dashes and Arabic digits are fine). The server saves it as `+201XXXXXXXXX`.
- `code` (string, required): the code from the reset SMS.
- `password` (string, required): 8 to 64 characters.
- `password_confirmation` (string, required): the same password again.

### Success

**200** with `message` ("Your password has been reset."). Go to Login. The user is signed out of every device, and the phone counts as verified.

**Next:** Show "Password changed" and go to Login.

### Errors

- **422:** The same error for a wrong code, an expired code, a used code, a code with too many wrong tries (5 per code) and an unknown phone: `errors.code` = "The code is wrong or has expired…". Show it under the code input and offer **Resend code**. Password errors come under `errors.password`.
- **429:** too many attempts from this phone number or this IP address (users on the same network share the IP limit). Wait for `Retry-After` seconds, then let the user retry.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Use the code from **Forgot password** (purpose `reset_password`); a sign-up code doesn't work here.
- Limits: 5 tries per phone number and 20 per IP address every 60 minutes (users on the same network share the IP limit). **Verify phone** and **Reset password** share one limit per phone.

item.name: 3. Account
item.description:
The logged-in user's screens:

1. **Home** and **Profile**: call **Get my account** on open (and pull to refresh). It gives the name, phone, account type, the national ID status and, for business accounts, the business profile status.
2. **Change password** screen: current password, new password, new password again → **Change password**.
3. **Settings › Log out**: first **Remove push token** (Push notifications), then **Log out**, then clear the stored token and go to Login.

request.description:
### What it does

Returns the logged-in user with everything the account screens need.

### Screen

**Home** and **Profile** screens, on open and on pull to refresh; also after the app starts with a stored token.

### Who can call it

Any logged-in user who is not blocked (customer, business or staff).

### Request

- No body. Send the Bearer token (mobile) or the session cookie (web).

### Success

**200** with `data`, the user: `id`, `name`, `phone`, `email`, `account_type` (`individual` | `business`), `register_as` (`business` | `tayar`, or null for accounts from before sign up asked for it), `next_step` (the screen to open: see **Get my account**), `locale` (`ar` | `en`), `status` (`active` | `blocked`), `is_phone_verified`, `phone_verified_at`, `national_id` (`status`: null | `pending` | `approved` | `rejected`, `rejection_reason`, `verified_at`, `front` and `back` files with a signed `url`), `business_profile` (or null), `last_mode` (`client` | `tayar`: the mode the app reopens in), `tayar_profile` (`id`, `status`, `is_online`, `rejection_reason`, `can_reapply_at`, or null when the user never applied), `roles` (staff role names, for display only; an empty list for customers) and `permissions` (what the user may do; an empty list for customers, every permission for a super admin).

`next_step` says which screen to open, also after a reinstall or a login on another phone:
- `complete_business_profile`: the business profile form → **Create business profile**.
- `business_under_review`: the "waiting for review" screen (**Get business profile**).
- `business_rejected`: show `business_profile.rejection_reason` and let the user fix the data or documents (**Update business profile**, **Upload document**).
- `complete_tayar_application`: the tayar application form → **Get vehicle types**, then **Apply to be a tayar**.
- `tayar_under_review`: the "waiting for review" screen (**Get my tayar application**).
- `tayar_rejected`: show `tayar_profile.rejection_reason`; changes are allowed from `tayar_profile.can_reapply_at`.
- `ready`: the home screen. Staff are always `ready`; older accounts without `register_as` are `ready` unless they are a business account or have a tayar application.

**Next:** For business accounts, show the business profile status from `business_profile`; show the national ID status from `national_id`.

### Errors

- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** the account is blocked (`message` says so). Show the message and log the user out.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- `next_step` follows only the side the user registered as (`register_as`); an application on the other side shows in its own status (`business_profile`, `tayar_profile`).
- A tayar reaching `ready` is still in client mode (`last_mode` = `client`): call **Switch mode** with `tayar` once before **Go online**.
- The document `url`s expire after 5 minutes: call **me** again to refresh them.

### What it does

Changes the password of the logged-in user.

### Screen

**Change password** screen, when the user taps **Save**.

### Who can call it

Any logged-in user who is not blocked.

### Request

- `current_password` (string, required): the current password, up to 64 characters.
- `password` (string, required): the new password, 8 to 64 characters, different from the current one.
- `password_confirmation` (string, required): the new password again.

### Success

**200** with `message` ("Your password has been changed."). The user stays logged in here; their other mobile logins are signed out.

**Next:** Show "Password changed" and go back. Other phones of this user are logged out.

### Errors

- **422:** `errors.current_password` (wrong current password) or `errors.password` (too short, too long, not confirmed, or the same as the current one).
- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** the account is blocked (`message` says so). Show the message and log the user out.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- From the web, every mobile login of this user is signed out (the web session stays).

### What it does

Logs out: on mobile it deletes the current token; on the web it ends the session.

### Screen

**Settings**, when the user taps **Log out** (after **Remove push token**).

### Who can call it

Any logged-in user, blocked users too.

### Request

- No body.

### Success

**200** with `message` ("You have been logged out."). Clear the stored login and go to Login.

**Next:** Clear the stored token and go to Login.

### Errors

- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login. (treat it as already logged out)
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Even if the call fails, clear the stored login on the device.

item.name: 4. Push notifications
item.description:
Keep the FCM push token on the server:

1. After every successful login, get the FCM token and call **Save push token** with the platform and app version.
2. When FCM gives a new token (`onTokenRefresh`), call **Save push token** again.
3. On logout, call **Remove push token** **before** **Log out**, while the login is still valid.
4. Ask for notification permission (iOS, and Android 13 and later) before getting the token.

**What the app receives.** Every push is sent to all of the user's saved devices, through FCM:

- `notification.title` and `notification.body`: already in the user's language (`locale`), so show them as they are.
- `data`: every value is a **string**. There is always a `type`; each type adds its own keys. Ignore a `type` the app does not know. The types so far:

| `data.type` | Sent to | Other keys | Open |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `test` | the user (server `push:test` command) | none | nothing |
| `order_offer` | a tayar, for a new offer | `order_id`, `offer_id` | the work screen, then **Get my offers** at once (the offer lasts 60 seconds) |
| `order_accepted` | the sender, when a tayar accepts | `order_id` | **Order details** (client mode) |
| `order_no_tayar` | the sender, when no tayar accepted in time and the order was cancelled | `order_id` | **Order details** (client mode) |
| `order_cancelled` | the tayar of an accepted order the sender or staff cancelled | `order_id`, `cancelled_by_type` (`sender` or `staff`) | **My order** (tayar mode) |
| `order_picked_up` | the sender, when the tayar picked the order up | `order_id` | **Order details** (client mode) |
| `order_on_the_way` | the sender, when the receiver confirmed and the order is on the way | `order_id` | **Order details** (client mode) |
| `order_delivered` | the sender, when the receiver's delivery code was accepted | `order_id` | **Order details** (client mode) |
| `order_not_delivered` | the sender; also the tayar when staff close the order (receiver unreachable) | `order_id` | **Order details** (client mode) or **My order** (tayar mode) |
- Android uses the default notification channel (no `channel_id` is sent). If the app later creates its own channel, the server can send its id.

**Handling it:**

- App open (`FirebaseMessaging.onMessage`): FCM shows nothing by itself, so show a local notification or an in-app banner.
- App in the background (`onMessageOpenedApp`) or closed (`getInitialMessage()` on start): when the user taps the notification, open the screen for `data.type`. Ignore a `type` the app does not know.

A token that FCM reports as unregistered or invalid is removed on the server, so keep calling **Save push token** after login and on every token refresh.

request.description:
### What it does

Saves the FCM push token of this device, so the user gets push notifications.

### Screen

No screen: right after login, and whenever FCM refreshes the token.

### Who can call it

Any logged-in user who is not blocked.

### Request

- `platform` (required): `android`, `ios` or `web`.
- `push_token` (string, required): the FCM token, up to 255 characters.
- `app_version` (string, optional): up to 20 characters, for example `1.4.0`.

### Success

**201** when the token is new, **200** when it was already saved. `data`: `id`, `platform`, `app_version`, `last_seen_at`. The push token itself is never returned.

### Errors

- **422:** field errors.
- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** the account is blocked (`message` says so). Show the message and log the user out.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- One token belongs to one device: if it was saved for another user (someone else logged in on this phone before), it moves to the current user.

### What it does

Removes the FCM push token of this device, so it stops getting this user's notifications.

### Screen

No screen: on **Log out**, just before calling **Log out**.

### Who can call it

Any logged-in user who is not blocked.

### Request

- `push_token` (string, required): the same FCM token. Send it as a query parameter (or in the body).

### Success

**204** with no body. It also answers 204 when the token was not saved for this user.

### Errors

- **422:** `push_token` is missing.
- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** the account is blocked (`message` says so). Show the message and log the user out.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Call it **before** logout: after logout the token is no longer valid.

item.name: 5. Business profile
item.description:
Business accounts (`account_type` = `business`; new sign ups have `register_as` = `business`):

1. **Business profile** screen: on open → **Get business profile**. A 404 means there is no profile yet: show the form.
2. Show the status banner: **pending** ("waiting for review"), **approved**, or **rejected** with `rejection_reason`.
3. **Business profile form**: load the type picker with **Get business types**. On first submit → **Create business profile** (multipart, with both national ID sides and, optionally, the commercial register (السجل التجاري) and the tax card (البطاقة الضريبية)). Later edits → **Update business profile** (JSON, no files).
4. **Documents** screen: one row per document with its current file; **Upload** or **Replace** → **Upload document**.
5. Changing the business name, type or tax number, or any document, sends an approved or rejected profile back to pending: warn before saving.

request.description:
### What it does

Lists the active business types (restaurant, pharmacy, …) for the business type picker.

### Screen

**Business profile form**, on open, to fill the business type picker.

### Who can call it

Anyone, no login.

### Request

- Query `per_page` (optional, 1 to 100, default 20) and `page` (optional, starts at 1).
- `Accept-Language` decides the language of the names.

### Success

**200** with `data`: a list of `{ id, name }` in display order, plus `meta` and `links` for pages.

### Errors

- **422:** `per_page` is out of range.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Send the chosen `id` as `business_type_id` in the business profile form, not at sign up. Load the list again when the user changes the language.

### What it does

Returns the business profile of the logged-in business account, with its review status.

### Screen

**Business profile** screen, on open and on pull to refresh.

### Who can call it

A logged-in customer account (not staff) with a business profile.

### Request

- No body.

### Success

**200** with `data`, the business profile: `id`, `business_type` (`id`, `name`), `business_name`, `description`, `avg_daily_orders`, `tax_registration_number`, `verification_status` (`pending` | `approved` | `rejected`), `rejection_reason`, `reviewed_at`, `links` (`id`, `type`, `url`), `documents` (`national_id_front`, `national_id_back`, `commercial_register` (the commercial register, السجل التجاري), `tax_card` (the tax card, البطاقة الضريبية): each a file with `file_name`, `mime_type`, `size`, `uploaded_at` and a signed `url`, or null), `created_at`, `updated_at`.

### Errors

- **404:** no business profile yet: show the create form or the onboarding.
- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** `message` explains why: the account is blocked, the phone is not verified yet (when phone verification is on), or a staff account tried a customer screen. Show the message; for "verify your phone", send the user to the OTP screen.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Show the status: `pending` = waiting for review; `approved` = ready; `rejected` = show `rejection_reason` and let the user fix the data or the documents.
- Document `url`s expire after 5 minutes.

### What it does

Creates the business profile, with the documents, in one multipart request. It starts as `pending`.

### Screen

**Business profile form**, the first time the user taps **Submit**.

### Who can call it

A logged-in **business** account without a business profile yet.

### Request

Send `multipart/form-data`:
- `business_type_id` (number, required): an `id` from the business types list.
- `business_name` (string, required): up to 255 characters.
- `description` (string, optional): up to 2000 characters.
- `avg_daily_orders` (number, optional): 0 to 100000.
- `tax_registration_number` (string, optional): up to 50 characters.
- `links` (optional, up to 10): `links[0][type]` (`website`, `facebook`, `instagram`, `tiktok`, `whatsapp` or `other`) and `links[0][url]` (a full URL, up to 2048 characters).
- `national_id_front` and `national_id_back` (files, required): jpg, jpeg, png, webp or pdf, up to 5 MB.
- `commercial_register` (the commercial register, السجل التجاري) and `tax_card` (the tax card, البطاقة الضريبية) (files, optional): jpg, jpeg, png, webp or pdf, up to 5 MB.

### Success

**201** with `data`, the new business profile: `id`, `business_type` (`id`, `name`), `business_name`, `description`, `avg_daily_orders`, `tax_registration_number`, `verification_status` (`pending` | `approved` | `rejected`), `rejection_reason`, `reviewed_at`, `links` (`id`, `type`, `url`), `documents` (`national_id_front`, `national_id_back`, `commercial_register` (the commercial register, السجل التجاري), `tax_card` (the tax card, البطاقة الضريبية): each a file with `file_name`, `mime_type`, `size`, `uploaded_at` and a signed `url`, or null), `created_at`, `updated_at`. Show the "waiting for review" state.

**Next:** Open the Business profile screen with the "waiting for review" banner.

### Errors

item.name: 9. Tayar mode · Switch mode
item.description:
Moving between client mode and tayar mode:

1. **Mode switch** in the account menu (only when `tayar_profile.status` is `approved`) → **Switch mode** with `tayar` or `client`.
2. The app reopens in `last_mode` next time.
3. Switch to tayar mode **before** going online: **Go online** answers 403 while the app is in client mode.
4. Approval doesn't change the mode: when `register_as` = `tayar`, `next_step` = `ready` and `last_mode` = `client`, call **Switch mode** with `tayar` once, without asking the tayar.

item.name: 10. Tayar mode · Go online and offline
item.description:
The tayar home screen toggle, with the mode picker:

1. The tayar home is only shown in tayar mode (after **Switch mode** with `tayar`; a newly approved tayar with `last_mode` = `client` switches once first).
2. **Online** toggle on → the **Choose mode** sheet → **Get modes**: one card per mode with `name` and `description`.
3. After the tayar picks a mode, ask for what it needs, from its flags:
   - `requires_area` → the **Area picker** → **Get areas** (circles on the map from `center` and `radius_km`);
   - `requires_radius` → a **radius slider** from `radius_km.min` to `radius_km.max` km;
   - `requires_destination` → a **destination picker** on the map (address, lat, lng).
4. Read the GPS position → **Go online** with `mode_id` and the field the mode needs. Then start the background location service (**Location updates**).
5. **Change mode** while online → the same sheet, then **Go online** again with the new settings: the server ends the old work session and starts a new one. Same settings only move the position.
6. **Online** toggle off → **Go offline**, then stop the location service. While the tayar holds an accepted, picked-up or ongoing order, going offline (and switching to client mode) answers 422: keep working and keep the location service running.
7. `is_online` in **Get my account** (`tayar_profile.is_online`) tells the toggle state when the app opens; `work_session.mode` in the **Go online** response tells the current mode.

item.name: 11. Tayar mode · Location updates
item.description:
A background service while online:

1. Send **Update location** every 5 to 10 seconds, also when the app is in the background. At most 20 a minute.
2. On **429**, wait for `Retry-After` seconds and send only the latest position (drop the ones in between).
3. On **422** `errors.status` (offline), stop the service and show the offline state: the server sets a tayar offline after 5 minutes without a location.

**New order › Category** step, on open.

item.name: 14. Client mode · Orders
item.description:
Sending and following orders, for **approved business accounts** (`next_step` = `ready`; individual customers come later). Other accounts get **403** with a message: show it with a link to the business profile.

1. **New order** flow: category (**Get categories**, folder 13) → pickup and drop-off on the map → **Estimate price** (call it again whenever the category or a point changes) → receiver, goods value, who pays the shipping, details → **Create order** with the `shipping_fee` the user saw.
2. Make one `idempotency_key` (UUID) when the New order screen opens and keep it for every retry of **Create order**. A 200 means the order already existed: open it as if it were new.
3. A 422 on `shipping_fee` means the price changed: show the new price from the message, ask again, and send the new `shipping_fee` with the same key.
4. **My orders** screen: two tabs, Active and Past → **Get my orders** with `status` = `active` or `past`. Infinite scroll with `cursor` = `meta.next_cursor`.
5. **Order details** → **Get order**. Show **Cancel order** while `can_cancel` is true.
6. **Cancel** dialog → **Get cancel reasons**, then **Cancel order** with the picked reason and an optional note.
7. While `status` = `looking_for_tayar`, **Order details** shows "Looking for a tayar…" until `search_ends_at`, and calls **Get order** again every 10 seconds while it is open (and when an `order_accepted` or `order_no_tayar` push arrives).
8. When a tayar accepts (`status` = `pending`), show the `tayar` card: name, a call button for `phone`, and the vehicle (`type`, `model`, `color`, `plate_number`). **Cancel order** stays until pickup: free until `free_cancel_until` (120 seconds), then the **Cancel** dialog shows the fee from `cancel_fee_now`, owed to the tayar.
9. `cancelled_by_type` = `system`: no tayar accepted in time. Show "No tayar found" with a **Send again** button that opens New order with the same details and a new `idempotency_key`.
10. From acceptance to delivery, **Order details** shows the tayar on a map from `tayar.location` (with how old `updated_at` is) and the steps: picked up (with the pickup photos), on the way, delivered or not delivered (with the reason). Poll **Get order** every 10 to 15 seconds while the screen is open, and on `order_picked_up`, `order_on_the_way`, `order_delivered` and `order_not_delivered` pushes. There is no ETA.
11. After pickup nobody can cancel. The receiver gets the codes and the tracking link by SMS (only once a real SMS provider is configured); a **Share tracking link** button can build it from `tracking_token`. Delivery does not check payment yet.

### What it does

Prices a trip before the order is created. Nothing is saved.

### Screen

**New order › Price** step, after both points are on the map, and again when the category or a point changes.

### Who can call it

An approved business account (individual customers come later).

### Request

- `category_id` (number, required): a subcategory from **Get categories** (one of a main category's `children`).
- `pickup_lat`, `pickup_lng`, `dropoff_lat`, `dropoff_lng` (numbers, required): the points picked on the map, up to 7 decimals.

### Success

**200** with `data`: `{ distance_km, food_extra, shipping_fee }`, strings with two decimals (km and EGP). Show `shipping_fee` as the price, and keep it to send with **Create order**.

### Errors

- **422:** field errors.
- **422:** `errors.route`: the pickup and drop-off are less than 100 m apart (in a straight line), the drop-off is more than 1200 km (by road) from the pickup, Tayari does not deliver on this route yet, or a food order is too far (food only goes up to 15 km, or inside one area). Show it on the map step.
- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** `message` explains why: only business accounts can send orders for now, or the business profile is not approved yet. Show the message with a link to the business profile page.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- The price is the larger of the minimum fare and the base fare + price per km × distance, plus a food extra for food categories. The distance is the straight line times a road factor, so it is a little longer than on the map.
- The customer never picks a mode: Tayari picks it from the trip.
- Call it again whenever the category or a point changes.

### What it does

Creates an order at the price from **Estimate price**. The order starts in `looking_for_tayar`.

### Screen

**New order › Confirm** step, when the user taps **Send order**.

### Who can call it

An approved business account (individual customers come later).

### Request

- `idempotency_key` (string, required): a UUID made once when the order form opens, and sent again on every retry of the same order.
- `category_id` (number, required): a subcategory from **Get categories** (one of a main category's `children`).
- `pickup_lat`, `pickup_lng`, `dropoff_lat`, `dropoff_lng` (numbers, required): the points picked on the map, up to 7 decimals.
- `details` (string, optional, up to 2000 characters): what is in the package.
- `pickup_address`, `dropoff_address` (strings, required, up to 255 characters).
- `pickup_contact_phone` (string, optional): someone to call at the pickup, if not the sender; any Egyptian mobile format.
- `receiver_name` (string, required, up to 255 characters) and `receiver_phone` (string, required, any Egyptian mobile format).
- `goods_value` (required): the price of the goods the receiver pays, 0 to 1000000, up to 2 decimals.
- `shipping_paid_by` (required): `sender` or `receiver`.
- `shipping_fee` (required): the `shipping_fee` from **Estimate price**, as shown to the user.

### Success

**201** with `data`, the new order: `id`, `code` (the short code people see, e.g. `TY-7K3P9Q`), `status` (`looking_for_tayar` | `pending` | `picked_up` | `ongoing` | `delivered` | `not_delivered` | `cancelled`), `can_cancel` (true until pickup), `category` (`id`, `name`, `is_food`), `details`, `pickup` (`address`, `lat`, `lng`, `contact_phone`), `dropoff` (`address`, `lat`, `lng`), `receiver` (`name`, `phone`), `goods_value`, `shipping_paid_by` (`sender` | `receiver`), `amount_to_collect` (what the receiver pays: the goods value, plus the shipping fee when the receiver pays it), `distance_km`, `food_extra`, `shipping_fee`, `cancel_reason` (`id`, `name`, or null), `tayar` (null until a tayar accepts; then `name`, `phone` (null once the order is delivered, not delivered or cancelled) and `vehicle` (`type`, `model`, `color`, `plate_number`)), `cancelled_by_type` (null unless cancelled; then `sender`, `staff`, or `system` when no tayar accepted in time), `free_cancel_until` (while `pending`: until when cancelling is free; otherwise null), `cancel_fee_now` (what cancelling now would cost: `"0.00"` before a tayar accepts and until `free_cancel_until`, then the cancellation fee, at most the shipping fee), `cancel_fee` (the fee recorded when the order was cancelled, `"0.00"` otherwise), `search_ends_at` (while `looking_for_tayar`: when Tayari stops looking and cancels the order; otherwise null), `price_accepted_at`, `accepted_at` (when the tayar accepted, or null), `cancelled_at`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Amounts are strings with two decimals, in EGP; coordinates are strings with 7 decimals. Delivery: `tayar.location` (`lat`, `lng`, `updated_at`: the tayar's last position while the order is `pending`, `picked_up` or `ongoing`, otherwise null), `pickup_photos` (the tayar's photos at pickup, each with a signed `url`), `picked_up_at`, `receiver_confirmed_at`, `codes_sent_at` (when the receiver's codes were last sent by SMS), `delivered_at`, `not_delivered_at`, `not_delivered_reason` (`id`, `name`, or null), `not_delivered_note`, `tracking_token` (for the receiver's tracking link). **200** with the same order when this `idempotency_key` already made one (a double tap or a retry).

**Next:** Open **Order details** for the returned order (201 or 200).

### Errors

- **422:** field errors. When the price changed since the estimate: `errors.shipping_fee` = "The shipping price is now 45.00 EGP. Check the new price and confirm again." Show the new price and ask the user to confirm again (send the new `shipping_fee` with the same `idempotency_key`). When the order this `idempotency_key` made was deleted: `errors.idempotency_key` = "This request key belongs to a deleted order. Use a new request key." Make a new key and send again.
- **422:** `errors.route`: the pickup and drop-off are less than 100 m apart (in a straight line), the drop-off is more than 1200 km (by road) from the pickup, Tayari does not deliver on this route yet, or a food order is too far (food only goes up to 15 km, or inside one area). Show it on the map step.
- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** `message` explains why: only business accounts can send orders for now, or the business profile is not approved yet. Show the message with a link to the business profile page.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Disable the **Send** button while the request runs, but keep the same `idempotency_key` for retries: the server never creates two orders for one key. Make a new key only for a new order.
- Phones come back as `+201XXXXXXXXX`.
- The search for a tayar starts at once: the order is offered to up to 5 nearby tayars at a time, each offer lasting 60 seconds, in a wider circle each round around the pickup (3 km, then 3 km more each round, up to 10 km; a round with nobody in reach widens at once). When no tayar accepts by `search_ends_at` (15 minutes after the price was accepted), Tayari cancels the order (`cancelled_by_type` = `system`) and sends an `order_no_tayar` push.

item.name: 17. Tayar mode · Delivery
item.description:
The steps after accepting an order (folder 16 shows it). Every step sends the current GPS `lat`/`lng`.

1. **At the pickup:** photograph the items → **Confirm pickup** with 1 to 4 photos (multipart). The receiver then gets the delivery and refusal codes and the tracking link by SMS; `receiver_codes.sent_at` shows when. From now on nobody can cancel.
2. **Call the receiver.** When they confirm they are there today → **Receiver confirmed**: the order is on the way. Receiver unreachable or not there today: don't confirm; contact support, who closes the order as not delivered (you get an `order_not_delivered` push).
3. **At the drop-off:** the receiver reads out the delivery code → **Deliver** with `code`. If they refuse the order, they read out the refusal code → **Get not-delivered reasons**, then **Mark not delivered** with `code`, the reason and an optional note. Not delivered is final for now; contact support about returning the goods.
4. **Wrong codes:** both steps share 5 tries; `receiver_codes.attempts_left` counts down. When `receiver_codes.problem` is `codes_locked` or `codes_expired`, ask the receiver to request new codes from their tracking link, or contact support.
5. While holding an order the tayar can't go offline or switch to client mode, and the server never sets them offline: keep the location service running, because the sender and the receiver see the last position.
6. Delivery does not check payment yet: the payment phase comes later. The receiver gets codes only once a real SMS provider is configured on the server.

item.name: 2. Sign up and login
item.description:
From a visitor to a logged-in user:

1. On app load (and before **Log in**), call **Get CSRF cookie**.
2. **Sign up** page: name, phone, password, password again → **Sign up** with `register_as` = `business` (the website signs up business owners only for now).
3. If `phone_verification_required` is true, open the **OTP** page; otherwise go to **Login**.
4. **OTP** page: code input and a **Resend code** link with a countdown from `resend_available_in` → **Verify phone** / **Resend code**.
5. **Login** page: phone and password → **Log in**. Then load **Get my account** and open the page for `next_step` (`complete_business_profile` → the onboarding wizard; `business_under_review` / `business_rejected` → the business profile page; `complete_tayar_application` / `tayar_under_review` / `tayar_rejected` → a "continue in the Tayari app" page, since the website is for business accounts only; `ready` → the account).
6. **Forgot password** page → **Forgot password**, then always the **Reset password** page → **Reset password**, then Login.

A 419 answer means the CSRF cookie is old: call **Get CSRF cookie** again and retry once.
